# Instagram

Generated from [tokens.json](tokens.json) and [README.md](README.md) by the design-systems catalog tool. Do not edit this file: change the tokens through the package's builders, then run `make design-md` at the repository root.

It follows the DESIGN.md spec, version alpha. That format has no themes, no per-value provenance and only px, em and rem units, so this file holds the `light` theme alone with every alias resolved. [tokens.json](tokens.json) is the source of truth: it records where each value was read, holds the `dark` theme, and keeps the 9 tokens from these groups that DESIGN.md cannot hold (gradients, shadows, percentages, durations and other non-colour or non-px values).

## Overview

Good for: Public signed-out Instagram: white or near-black page, one blue pill for the enabled action, 12px fields, directory lists.

Captured 2026-11-22, signed out. Themes: light, dark.

A token set and component reference for Instagram on the web, captured signed out from `https://www.instagram.com/` on 2026-11-22. Headless Chromium, desktop 1440x900 at 1x and phone 390x844 at 2x, light and dark. Dark is `color-scheme: dark`, which sets `html.__fb-dark-mode`. Light sets `html.__fb-light-mode`. There is no public theme switch.

The homepage is a login wall. Public pages that loaded are the locations directory, one country page, Popular, Instagram Lite, the official profile `instagram`, and the 404 page. Login, signup, and password reset were photographed empty and not submitted. Facebook and Meta Verified were recorded and not entered.

### Fonts (from README.md)

`--font-family-system-prism` is `"Instagram Sans UI", -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif`. Instagram Sans UI is Instagram's face and is not committed. The hero on the login page computed as "Instagram Sans Regular" at 40.32px. Body labels on the form computed as Optimistic at 15px / 500. Optimistic is not in the custom properties that resolved, so it is not a token. Fall back to the system stack in `core.font.family.system`.

## Do's and Don'ts

- Do take values from [tokens.json](tokens.json) when you need another theme, a value's source, or a token this file leaves out.
- Do read [README.md](README.md) before relying on a value; it says what is known to be wrong.
- Don't read colours off the screenshots; they are 256-colour PNGs.
- Don't copy the product's logo, icons, illustrations or brand colours into something that ships. Borrow structure and proportions.
- Don't edit this file; it is regenerated from the tokens.

### What to distrust (from README.md)

- The login "Log in" button in the screenshots is the disabled wash. Both fields were empty. The enabled blue is the token `light.color.button.primary.background` (`#4a5df9`), not the pixels of that crop.
- Screenshots are 256-colour PNGs. Read colours from tokens.json.
- The phone profile capture is the app-install sheet over a dimmed profile. Hiding that sheet left a blank page, so the sheet is the phone state.
- A bio links dialog was opened and then left out of the package. It contained private handles. It is not in `screenshots/`.
- Hover and pressed button fills are tokenised from CSS and were not photographed.

### Do and don't (from README.md)

- **Do** keep the page white in light and `#0c1014` in dark. The login split and the directory header both sit on `color.primary.background`.
- **Do** use one blue for the enabled action. The nav "Log In" pill and the enabled login button share `color.button.primary.background`.
- **Don't** treat the empty-form login button as the brand blue. That crop is the disabled wash.
- **Do** keep fields as 12px pills with a 1px stroke. The login form stacks two of them.
- **Don't** follow a control that asks for a password, a phone number, or Facebook. Those branches stop. See [site-tree.md](site-tree.md).
- **Don't** copy the glyph logo or the phone mock into something that ships. Borrow the split, the pill, and the type sizes.
